festivals.name: Rathotsavam
festivals.summary: A festival procession in which the deity is taken through the streets on a decorated temple car, drawn by devotees.
festivals.about: In many South Indian temples, a Rathotsavam is the high point of the festival season, with the deity drawn through the streets on a decorated car. Whether and when this temple observes it will be confirmed by the Trust.
festivals.participation: Participation and darshan arrangements will be shared by the temple office.
festivals.imageAlt: Crowds of devotees gathered around a decorated temple car during a festival procession
festivals.imageAlt2: Caparisoned elephants with golden face ornaments and red umbrellas in a festival procession

festivals.name: Annual Utsavam
festivals.summary: A multi-day annual celebration with special worship, processions and community gatherings around the temple.
festivals.about: An annual utsavam is usually spread over several days, with special rituals, processions and gatherings. The festival programme for this temple will be published once the Trust confirms it.
festivals.participation: Volunteering and offering details will be shared by the temple office.
festivals.imageAlt: A festival day outside a South Indian temple, with a tall gopuram and crowds of visitors in colourful clothes
festivals.imageAlt2: A crowd gathered around decorated elephants during a temple festival

festivals.name: Festive Kolam and Decoration
festivals.summary: Colourful kolam, flowers and lamps that adorn the temple and its surroundings on festive days.
festivals.about: Kolam, floral garlands and rows of lamps are a common part of festive days at South Indian temples. The occasions the temple decorates for will be confirmed by the Trust.
festivals.participation: Details on helping with decorations will be shared by the temple office.
festivals.imageAlt: A large circular floral rangoli in bright colours laid out on the floor for a festival
festivals.imageAlt2: A brass temple panel with a row of oil lamps and auspicious animals

sevas.name: Archana
sevas.summary: A personal offering of prayers and the recitation of the deity's names on behalf of a devotee or family.

sevas.name: Abhishekam
sevas.summary: A ritual bathing of the deity with sacred offerings, sponsored by devotees on special occasions.

sevas.name: Alankaram
sevas.summary: Special adornment of the deity with flowers, garlands and ornaments.

sevas.name: Lamp Offering
sevas.summary: Lighting lamps in the temple as an act of devotion, for a loved one or a special intention.

sevas.name: Annadanam
sevas.summary: Sponsoring a meal offered to devotees, a long-standing act of service at temples.

faqs.q: How can I make a contribution?
faqs.a: Please contact the Temple Office. They will give you the verified ways to contribute. Official details will appear on this page only after the Trust has confirmed them.

faqs.q: How do I know payment details are genuine?
faqs.a: Use only details given to you directly by the Temple Office. If anyone else sends you payment details for the temple, please check with the office before sending money.
Whether and how receipts are issued is confirmed by the Temple Office. Please ask when you enquire.

faqs.q: Can I give towards a particular purpose?
faqs.a: You can ask the Temple Office whether a contribution can be directed to a purpose such as daily worship, annadanam, temple upkeep or festivals.

faqs.q: Can I help in other ways?
faqs.a: Ask the Temple Office what the temple can accept and where help is needed.
